mechanism_interpretation: The full Magentic-One Orchestrator owns whole-team task/facts/plan/progress state, directs agents, detects stalls/loops and can reset/replan. Replacing it with a simple next-speaker selector removes progress tracking, loop detection and explicit direction and is reported to reduce GAIA validation performance by 31%.
why_proxy_not_direct: GAIA, AssistantBench and WebArena score broad end-task success rather than current whole-system regulation as the target function. The Orchestrator ablation simultaneously changes S2-relevant coordination and S3-relevant control mechanisms.
non_claim: The raw task-success metrics and 31% ablation effect do not quantify an S3 maturity level and do not determine canonical S3=A.

mechanism_interpretation: Canonical LLaMAR S3 is the model-driven whole-team planner/action-control path over shared open/completed commitments and current robot state. The published 2-agent MAP-THOR module ablation changes that native current-control bundle: Actor-only reports SR/TR/C/B 0.33/0.67/0.91/0.59, Planner+Actor+Verifier reports 0.45/0.78/0.92/0.69, Planner+Actor+Corrector reports 0.67/0.91/0.97/0.84, and the full stack reports 0.66/0.91/0.97/0.82.
why_proxy_not_direct: MAP-THOR reports broad end-task outcomes rather than current-control performance as the target variable. The ablation changes Planner, Verifier and Corrector combinations rather than isolating one S3 decision/feedback right, and the paper does not identify the exact Git execution revision for every reported run.
non_claim: The published ablation is native S3-relevant proxy evidence only. It does not quantify S3 maturity, does not establish canonical S3=A, and does not create a matched S3 primary baseline.
